story: Houston ISD is converting campuses to an AI-era Future 2 model whose afternoons are screen-free, while the board policy on artificial intelligence still sits unadopted on the August 13th agenda.

claims.text: Houston ISD Superintendent Mike Miles framed the Future 2 model as a shift in what schools teach students to do.
claims.quote: "Schools must shift focus from 'what to know' to 'how to think,'" Miles said. "What is our competitive advantage in an AI-enabled world?"
claims.notes: The source has a COMMA inside the closing single quote, because the attribution follows. Use the comma form or do not use the quote.

claims.text: Houston ISD announced the Future 2 model in February 2026 as a launch of two schools, with C. Martinez and Gregg elementary schools converting to pre-K-8 for the 2026 to 2027 school year.
claims.quote: Houston ISD is preparing what Superintendent Mike Miles calls "the next stage in changing the American public education system" with the launch of two Future 2 schools. Beginning in the 2026-27 school year, C. Martinez and Gregg elementary schools will convert to pre-K-8 schools with a new curriculum model.
claims.notes: READ WITH c10. This is the FEBRUARY figure. Do not put two and nine on the same slide without dating both.

claims.text: Houston ISD reported that the first four hours of the Future 2 day follow the district's standard NES curriculum.
claims.quote: The first four hours of school follow the standard NES curriculum across the district to include reading, writing, math, science and Art of Thinking core subjects.
claims.notes: The core academics in the morning half of the story, and it is solid.

claims.text: Houston ISD divides the Future 2 day into three parts and runs instruction from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with optional programming until 6:00 p.m.
claims.quote: The curriculum separates the day into three parts, operating from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. with the option for students to continue programming time until 6:00 p.m.
claims.notes: The Future 2 site states building hours differently. Pick one source and quote its formatting exactly. Do not merge them.

claims.text: The Future 2 daily schedule sets a one hour coursework block focused on AI literacy and design thinking, a 110 minute experiences block, and a 90 minute workshop block.
claims.quote: Coursework (one hour), with a focus on AI literacy and design thinking courses
claims.notes: The source writes the coursework duration as the WORD one hour and the others as NUMERALS 110 minutes and 90 minutes. Reproduce that, do not regularise it. The source does NOT say which block falls in the afternoon.

claims.text: Houston ISD states that Future 2 afternoon experiences are screen-free.
claims.quote: Along with being screen-free, afternoon experiences provide enrichment opportunities that can cost thousands of dollars outside of school.
claims.source_publisher: Houston Independent School District (Future 2 Schools site)
claims.notes: THE CENTRAL FACT OF THIS DECK. The AI-era school puts the screens in the morning and takes them away after lunch. Source page is undated; published_date carries the date it was retrieved.

claims.text: Houston ISD describes a Future 2 school as one where students build academic foundations in the morning and pursue hands-on experiences and workshops in the afternoon.
claims.quote: A place where students build strong academic foundations in the morning and explore real-world interests through hands-on experiences and workshops in the afternoon, helping them develop the confidence, character, and life skills needed to thrive beyond the classroom.
claims.source_publisher: Houston Independent School District (Future 2 Schools site)
claims.notes: Undated page; published_date is the retrieval date. Verified verbatim on a second fetch after the first returned a summary.

claims.text: Houston ISD offers students in the top percentile on Measurement of Academic Progress tests an optional accelerated AI-driven learning platform for reading and math.
claims.quote: To increase academic rigor, students among the top percentile on Measurement of Academic Progress (MAP) tests will have the option to follow an accelerated, AI-driven learning platform for their reading and math courses.
claims.notes: The ONLY verified statement about an AI learning platform at Future 2. The district names NO vendor. Do not attach any vendor name to it.

claims.text: Houston ISD requires Future 2 students to clear an attendance rate and a national percentile benchmark to be promoted through the two-year dyad sequence.
claims.notes: The second benchmark reads verbatim: Score in at least the 40th percentile nationally on Measurement of Academic Progress (MAP) scores or accomplish meets or exceeds grade level scores on State of Texas Assessment for Academic Readiness (STAAR) for the reading and math exams. The figures are 93% and the 40th percentile.

claims.text: The Texan reported in May 2026 that Houston ISD would move nine campuses to the Future 2 model for the 2026 to 2027 school year.
claims.quote: Houston Independent School District (ISD) will transition nine campuses to the district's Future 2 program
claims.notes: JOURNALISM, NOT THE DISTRICT. The count nine is stated by no district page reachable this run. Quote trimmed before the school-year span, which in the source carries an en dash.

claims.text: Houston ISD's Future 2 site lists its campuses as five pairings covering Clemente Martinez, Gregg, Hartman, Bonham, Sugar Grove Academy, Shadydale, Forest Brook, Southmayd and Deady.
claims.source_publisher: Houston Independent School District (Future 2 Schools site)
claims.notes: The page STATES NO TOTAL. This claim may name the campuses but must NOT assert a number. If the deck needs the numeral nine it comes from c10 and is attributed to The Texan. Undated page; published_date is the retrieval date.

claims.text: Katy ISD assistant superintendent for teaching and learning Dr. Sanee Bell said the district has a responsibility to prepare students to use AI tools thoughtfully.
claims.quote: "Artificial intelligence is transforming the world our students will inherit, and it is our responsibility to prepare them to use these tools thoughtfully and with clear purpose," said Dr. Sanée Bell, assistant superintendent for teaching and learning.
claims.notes: VERIFIED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER. Her name carries an acute accent, Sanée.

claims.text: Katy ISD's framework states that AI is a tool and not a teacher, and that educators remain responsible for designing lessons and evaluating student learning.
claims.quote: Before AI becomes commonplace in classrooms, Katy ISD's framework addresses many questions families have about AI in schools by making it clear that AI is a tool, not a teacher. Katy ISD educators remain responsible for designing lessons, evaluating student learning, building relationships and making instructional decisions.
claims.notes: The phrase Before AI becomes commonplace in classrooms is the district signalling AI is not yet commonplace there. This is a contrast of PACE with Houston, never of prohibition. Katy bans nothing that could be verified.

claims.text: Katy ISD unveiled its Artificial Intelligence Framework at its July Board Work Study meeting and calls it a living resource expected to evolve.
claims.quote: The presentation also introduced Katy ISD's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Framework, a comprehensive guide for the responsible integration of AI across District classrooms.
claims.notes: The board presentation date is July 20th, 2026, item 9.2. The framework document itself could not be reached through eleven paths.

claims.text: Katy ISD reports kindergarten students spend about 35 minutes per week on technology skills. First and second graders spend about one hour per week, and fifth graders about 85 minutes per week.
claims.quote: At the kindergarten level, students spend about 35 minutes per week building foundational technology skills through the district's core curriculum and lessons and activities that directly address the state's TEKS for technology application. In first and second grade, that increases to about one hour per week.
claims.notes: The source says about one hour per week for grades 1 and 2, NOT 60 minutes. Do not convert it. These are TECHNOLOGY TEKS minutes, not AI minutes. Do not caption them as time spent on AI.

claims.text: Houston ISD board policy CQD(LOCAL) on artificial intelligence was on the School Board's August 13th, 2026 agenda for second reading and the record shows no passage.
claims.quote: Approval To Establish Board Policy CQD(LOCAL), Technology Resources: Artificial Intelligence-Second Reading
claims.notes: Verified across three endpoints. MatterFile 26-238, MatterStatusName Agenda Ready, MatterIntroDate 2026-06-15, MatterAgendaDate 2026-08-13, MatterPassedDate NULL, MatterEnactmentDate NULL. Event 1304 EventMinutesStatusName Draft. Agenda sequence 53 with action name, action text and passed flag all NULL. DO NOT WRITE THAT IT WAS ADOPTED. The verbatim title contains a colon, which house style forbids in our prose but a verbatim quote is exempt.

claims.text: Temple ISD superintendent Dr. Bobby Ott said the district will phase AI in for students this school year, after three years of staff training.
claims.quote: The gradual rollout comes after district staff spent the last three years training with the technology to ensure it is integrated safely and effectively.
claims.notes: JOURNALISM, label it as such. The source writes the last three years in WORDS. Do not render it as 3 years.

claims.text: Houston ISD cites a McKinsey and Company projection that 57% of jobs could be automated by 2030 as part of its rationale for Future 2.
claims.quote: Amid consulting firm McKinsey and Company's projection that 57% of jobs could be automated by 2030, the curriculum prioritizes interpersonal skills and real-world experiences alongside core academics to prepare students for work technology can't replace.
claims.notes: USE ONLY WITH ATTRIBUTION TO HISD. Verified as something HISD PUBLISHED, not as a verified McKinsey figure. The honest framing is that Houston ISD cites a projection. If the deck states 57% as a fact about the labour market, that must not ship.

rejected.reason: NOT IN THE PRIMARY SOURCE AT ALL. The full verbatim body of the July 20th post was pulled twice and contains no grade-level restriction, no prohibition, and no mention of Gemini or Copilot. The AI Framework document could not be located through eleven paths, all 404 or 403. This was the load-bearing claim of the original story and it is unsupported, so the two districts went opposite directions frame was abandoned.

rejected.reason: Came from a secondary blog. Neither name appears in the primary, nor does any curriculum-embedded platform concept.

rejected.reason: No grade-differentiated permission of any kind appears in the primary post.

rejected.what: An August 10th, 2026 start date, and an Alpha School TimeBack AI platform at Gregg and Clemente Martinez
rejected.reason: SOURCE UNREACHABLE. Every houstonpublicmedia.org URL returns 403, and the site root returns 403, so the block is site-wide. No reachable source states a TimeBack or Alpha School relationship. The district names only an unnamed accelerated AI-driven learning platform, which is c8.

rejected.what: An assessment threshold of above 60 percent
rejected.reason: CONTRADICTED BY THE SOURCE. The release states Over a 93% attendance rate and at least the 40th percentile nationally on MAP. There is no 60 percent figure anywhere in the document.

rejected.what: Teachers remain the teachers of record at Future 2
rejected.reason: Traces only to the 403'd houstonpublicmedia.org. The phrase appears in no reachable Houston source. The nearest verified language is Katy ISD's about its own educators, and attributing it to Houston would put the right sentence in the wrong district.

rejected.what: AI literacy and design thinking happen in the afternoon at Future 2
rejected.reason: CONTRADICTED. The district states afternoon experiences are screen-free, which is c6. The release places a one hour AI literacy block in the schedule but never assigns it to the afternoon.

rejected.what: Houston ISD board policy CQD(LOCAL) was adopted
rejected.reason: Guarded rather than dropped. MatterPassedDate and MatterEnactmentDate are both NULL, the item has no action name or text, and the minutes are Draft. Any copy saying adopted, approved or passed is unverified.

rejected.what: A single authoritative count of Future 2 campuses
rejected.reason: Sources disagree by date and will not be reconciled by arithmetic. HISD in February said two. The Texan in May said nine. The campuses page lists names and states no total.
